events.title: The victory of Lepanto
events.shortBlurb: The Holy League's fleet broke the Ottoman navy at Lepanto off the Greek coast; the day gave rise to the feast of the Rosary…
body: The battle was provoked by Cyprus: in 1570 the Turks seized the Venetian island, and after a long siege Famagusta fell in August 1571, its commander Bragadin flayed alive. Pius V bound Spain, Venice, and the papal states into a Holy League whose two hundred galleys and six galleasses were commanded by Don John of Austria, the Emperor Charles V's natural son; among its soldiers was Miguel de Cervantes.

On the morning of 7 October 1571 the fleets met in the Gulf of Patras, near Lepanto. In hours of close and savage fighting Cervantes was thrice wounded and lost the use of his left hand; the Turkish fleet was all but destroyed and its commander Ali Pasha slain. The League lost some eight thousand men, but freed more than ten thousand Christian captives from the Turkish oars.

In Rome, Pius V credited the deliverance to the Mother of God, invoked that day by the Rosary confraternities, and kept it with an annual feast. The victory broke the Ottoman name for invincibility at sea, yet the allies quarreled, winter closed in, and Cyprus was never retaken; two years later Venice made her own peace with the Sultan.

sources.text: Catholic Encyclopedia (1913), “Feast of the Holy Rosary”
